title: CSS Specificity
description: Understand CSS specificity rules and how styles cascade.

options.text: An ID selector (#header) has higher specificity than any number of class selectors
options.explanation: Specificity is calculated as (inline, IDs, classes, elements). One ID (0,1,0,0) beats any number of classes (0,0,N,0). So #header beats .nav.main.header. Only inline styles and !important override IDs.
!important overrides ALL normal specificity. When two !important declarations conflict, normal specificity rules apply between them. Overusing !important creates maintenance nightmares.

options.text: The order of CSS rules never matters if specificities are different
options.explanation: Order matters when specificities are EQUAL — the last rule wins. When specificities differ, the more specific rule wins regardless of order. Both specificity AND source order play roles.

options.text: Pseudo-classes like :hover have the same specificity as element selectors
options.explanation: Pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus, :nth-child) have the same specificity as class selectors (0,0,1,0). Pseudo-elements (::before, ::after) have the same specificity as element selectors (0,0,0,1).
